---
title: "Kubernetes Manifests as Nix Modules"
---

# Kubernetes Manifests as Nix Modules

Hand-written YAML that drifts from the image tag in CI is how Saturday pages start. The boring default is: **generate manifests from Nix (same pin as `.#image`), commit the generated YAML if the cluster cannot eval Nix, and skip Helm until a chart is forced on you**.

## Mental model

Nix can produce JSON/YAML for `kubectl apply`. Libraries (`nixidy`, `kubenix`, or a 40-line `writeText`) all do the same job: **one evaluation, one tag, one registry**.

The cluster still runs kubelet. Nix does not replace Kubernetes. It replaces the YAML copypaste.

```
flake  →  image tag + digest
       →  Deployment YAML with that digest
       →  kubectl apply --server-side
```

If the platform already speaks Helm only, next chapter. If you own the app, raw manifests are enough.

## Worked examples

### Case 1: A Deployment as JSON

Save as `k8s.nix`:

```nix
# k8s.nix
{ pkgs ? import <nixpkgs> {} }:

let
  image = "registry.desk.internal/desk-api:1.0.0";
  doc = {
    apiVersion = "apps/v1";
    kind = "Deployment";
    metadata = { name = "desk-api"; namespace = "desk"; };
    spec = {
      replicas = 2;
      selector.matchLabels.app = "desk-api";
      template = {
        metadata.labels.app = "desk-api";
        spec.containers = [
          {
            name = "desk-api";
            inherit image;
            ports = [ { containerPort = 8080; } ];
            resources.requests = { cpu = "50m"; memory = "64Mi"; };
          }
        ];
      };
    };
  };
in
pkgs.writeText "desk-api-deploy.json" (builtins.toJSON doc)
```

```bash
nix-build k8s.nix
python3 -m json.tool result | head
```

### Case 2: Same flake as the image

```nix
# flake.nix fragment
{
  inputs.nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-26.05";
  outputs = { self, nixpkgs }: {
    packages.x86_64-linux.manifests = import ./k8s.nix {
      pkgs = nixpkgs.legacyPackages.x86_64-linux;
    };
  };
}
```

Bump the tag in **one** place (an overlay attr `desk.imageTag`) and rebuild image + manifests together.

### Case 3: Apply

```bash
kubectl apply --server-side -f result
kubectl -n desk rollout status deploy/desk-api
```

`--server-side` plays nicer with fields you do not own. Dry-run first on a shared cluster:

```bash
kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f result
```

### Case 4: ConfigMap from Nix, not from kubectl create

```nix
# configmap.nix
{ pkgs ? import <nixpkgs> {} }:

pkgs.writeText "desk-cm.json" (builtins.toJSON {
  apiVersion = "v1";
  kind = "ConfigMap";
  metadata = { name = "desk-api"; namespace = "desk"; };
  data.WINDOW = "A";
})
```

Secrets still do not belong here. Use External Secrets / sealed-secrets / CSI — or do not put the password in git, same rule as the Nix store.

### Case 5: When the cluster cannot run Nix

```bash
nix build .#manifests
cp result generated/desk-api-deploy.json
git add generated/
```

CI diffs `git diff --exit-code generated/` so humans cannot "just kubectl edit" without updating the flake.

## The trap

The trap is **templating the image as `latest`**. Every node may run a different digest. Pin tag **and** digest (`image: repo@sha256:…`) when the registry supports it.

## The boring rule

- Manifests and image from one flake pin (nixpkgs 26.05).
- JSON/YAML generated; apply server-side.
- No passwords in ConfigMaps.
- Pin digests in production.
- Generate-and-commit if GitOps tools cannot eval Nix.

## Try this

1. Case 1, `jq .spec.replicas result`.
2. Change replicas to 3, rebuild, `diff` the JSON.
3. Put `image: …:latest` in a lab, list why you will not ship it.
4. Add a Service JSON next to the Deployment in the same file (list of docs or a YAML stream).
